'''Fosun International Limited''' is a Chinese [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] [[holding company]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fosun-international.com/en/company/ |title=BLANK |website=www.fosun-international.com |access-date=2008-02-06 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924014910/http://www.fosun-international.com/en/company/ |archive-date=24 September 2015 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Founded in 1992 by [[Guo Guangchang]] and four others, the company is headquartered in [[Shanghai]] and was [[Incorporation (business)|incorporated]] in [[Hong Kong]] in 2004. Its Co-CEOs are Chen Qiyu and Xu Xiaoliang. [[Wang Qunbin]] joined Guo Guangchang as co-chairman in early 2020.<ref name="Bloomberg:">{{cite web |last1=Zhao |first1=Shirley |title=Fosun Names Co-Chairman, Picks Two Presidents as Co-CEOs |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-02-21/fosun-names-wang-qunbin-co-chairman-two-presidents-as-co-ceos |publisher=Bloomberg |access-date=27 February 2020 |date=21 February 2020}}</ref> The company is located in over 35 countries and is one of the largest privately owned conglomerates in China. It was ranked 371st on the [[Forbes Global 2000]] ranking in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/global2000/#3c652d49335d |title=2020 Forbes Global 2000 |work=Forbes |access-date=20 June 2020}}</ref>

=== 2000s ===
In 2004, a new holding company of the group, '''Fosun International Limited''' was incorporated in Hong Kong. In July 2007, Fosun International was listed on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong as SEHK:656.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/74233bfe-9fa2-11e5-beba-5e33e2b79e46|title=SubChina's Warren Buffett' caught up in Beijing probe|last=Anderlini|first=Jamil|date=11 December 2015|website=www.ft.com|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/capital-goods/hkg-656/fosun-international-shares|title=Fosun International (SEHK:656) - Share price, News & Analysis|website=Simply Wall St|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>

=== 2010s ===
During 2011, the three major growth engines of Fosun, industrial profits, investment profits and asset management profits rose rapidly, enabling Fosun to make strides toward its vision of becoming "a premium investment group with a focus on China's growth momentum".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://media.corporate-ir.net/media_files/IROL/13/130462/PPT_2011_ENG_V20_Final.pdf|title=Fosun International Limited Annual Results 2011|date=March 2012|website=Media.corporate-ir.net|access-date=29 January 2020}}</ref>

From 2010 through 2015, Fosun spent billions buying foreign firms in the healthcare, tourism, fashion, and banking industries in the US and Europe. These included France's [[Club Med]], Britain's [[Thomas Cook Group]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thomas-cook-m-a-fosun-comment-idUSKBN0M20Q820150306|title=Britain's Thomas Cook soars after China's Fosun buys stake|date=2015-03-06|work=Reuters|access-date=2020-02-03|language=en}}</ref> Canada's [[Cirque du Soleil]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cirquedusoleil-m-a-tpg-idUSKBN0NB1AX20150420|title=Cirque du Soleil sells majority stake to U.S., Chinese investors|date=2015-04-20|work=Reuters|access-date=2020-02-03|language=en}}</ref> American clothing label [[St. John (clothing)|St John]], and Greek jeweler [[Folli Follie]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/news/business/21700406-chinas-leading-industrial-conglomerate-needs-shed-debt-bloated-still-bingeing|title=Bloated but still bingeing|newspaper=The Economist|issn=0013-0613|access-date=15 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=China's Fosun joins bidding war for Portuguese hospital operator|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-29321688|access-date=23 September 2014|work=BBC News|date=23 September 2014}}</ref> At the end of 2014 Fosun acquired the US insurer Meadowbrook for around $433 million, marking the first full purchase of a US insurer by a Chinese company.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/article/us-meadowbrook-ins-m-a-fosun-intl-idUSKBN0K81MH20141231 China's Fosun to buy U.S. insurer to help finance acquisition spree]. [[Reuters]], 30 December 2014</ref> Fosun also purchased Australian oil company [[Roc Oil Company|Roc Oil]], its first acquisition in the petroleum industry.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://blogs.wsj.com/moneybeat/2014/08/04/fosun-edges-out-competitor-for-australias-roc-oil/ | title=Fosun Edges Out Competitor for Australia's Roc Oil | publisher=The Wall Street Journal | date=4 August 2014 | access-date=14 April 2017}}</ref>

On 11 December 2015, the chairman of Fosun, [[Guo Guangchang]], was reported missing. Guo however reappeared on 14 December 2015 at a Fosun board of directors meeting. During his disappearance, Fosun requested that trading of shares be temporarily suspended.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-35068463 Chinese tycoon Guo Guangchang reported missing.], [[BBC News]], 11 December 2015. Retrieved 11 December 2015.</ref> The Fosun board of directors issued a statement saying that Guo was assisting in a government inquiry which, in their opinion, did not present a "material adverse impact" on Fosun's finances or operations.<ref>{{Cite news|title = Another turn of the screw|url = https://www.economist.com/news/business/21684147-detention-fosuns-boss-shows-even-chinas-biggest-tycoons-are-no-longer-safe|newspaper = The Economist|access-date = 30 December 2015|issn = 0013-0613}}</ref>

In July 2016, Fosun bought the English football club [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] from its previous owner [[Steve Morgan (businessman)|Steve Morgan]] for an estimated £45 million. Under Fosun's ownership, Wolves have progressed from being a mid table side in the [[Football League Championship]] (second tier of English football) to finishing seventh in the [[FA Premier League]], reaching an [[FA Cup]] semi-final and qualifying for the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2019-05-18|title=Wolves qualify for Europa League after Man City win FA Cup|language=en-gb|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48303846|access-date=2020-07-19}}</ref><ref name="Fosun Group Takes Over">{{cite news|title=Fosun Group Takes Over Wolves|url=http://www.wolves.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/news-fosun-group-takes-over-wolves-3198807.aspx|publisher=Wolverhampton Wanderers|date=21 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36852323 |title=Wolves bought by Chinese conglomerate Fosun International for £45m |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=21 July 2016 |access-date=30 July 2016}}</ref>

In 2016 Fosun began to invest in India.<ref name="The Hindu Business Line: Fosun eyes Indian start-ups with $200-m fund">{{cite web |last1=Pani |first1=Priyanka |title=Fosun eyes Indian start-ups with $200-m fund |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/fosun-eyes-indian-startups-with-200m-fund/article9211995.ece |publisher=The Hindu Business Line |access-date=24 February 2020 |date=12 October 2016}}</ref> [[Delhivery]] was one such investment made in 2017,<ref name="ETtech.com: Delhivery secures $30M from Fosun International">{{cite web |last1=Gooptu |first1=Biswarup |last2=Ganguly |first2=Payal |title=Delhivery secures $30M from Fosun International |url=https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/startups/delhivery-secures-30m-from-fosun-international/58783413 |website=ETtech.com |access-date=24 February 2020 |date=23 May 2017}}</ref> in addition to previous investments in [[MakeMyTrip]], India's largest online travel company and Gland Pharma.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Biswarup Gooptu |author2=Payal Ganguly |work=ET Tech |url=https://tech.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/startups/delhivery-secures-30m-from-fosun-international/58783413 | title=Delhivery secures $30M from Fosun International |publisher=[[The Economic Times]] |date=23 May 2017 |access-date=23 May 2017}}</ref> Fosun is also involved in the Indian real estate market.<ref name="The Economic Times: Enter the Dragon: China's Fosun International plans to invest $1 billion">{{cite web |last1=sharma |first1=Ravi Teja |title=Enter the dragon: China's Fosun International plans to invest $1 billion via realty private equity platform |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/enter-the-dragon-chinas-fosun-international-plans-to-invest-1-billion-via-realty-private-equity-platform/articleshow/54340153.cms |publisher=The Economic Times |access-date=24 February 2020 |date=15 September 2016}}</ref>

On 28 August 2019, [[Thomas Cook Group]] announced that the group "had agreed the main terms of a rescue package that will see Hong Kong's Fosun Tourism take over its tour operations and creditor banks and bondholders acquire its airline".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-thomas-cook-grp-investment-fosun/uk-holiday-firm-thomas-cook-agrees-key-terms-of-rescue-deal-idUKKCN1VI0JJ?il=0|title=Chinese poised to acquire world's oldest travel firm as Thomas Cook agrees key rescue terms|publisher=[[Reuters]] |date=28 August 2019 |access-date=28 August 2019}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In early November 2019, Fosun said it would purchase the Thomas Cook brand for £11m. The company viewed itself as a "potential saviour" by purchasing the name.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-50267453|title=Thomas Cook brand sold to Club Med owner Fosun for £11m|date=1 November 2019|work=BBC News|access-date=2 November 2019|quote=He said: "The acquisition of the Thomas Cook brand will enable the group to expand its tourism business building on the extensive brand awareness of Thomas Cook and the robust growth momentum of Chinese outbound tourism."}}</ref>

=== 2020s ===
In March 2020, the company acquired a 55.4% equity interest in French jewelry brand Djula.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Spencer|first1=Mimosa|date=2020-03-27|title=Fosun's Jewelry Unit Yuyuan to Buy Majority Stake in Djula|url=https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/fosuns-jewelry-unit-yuyuan-buy-majority-stake-djula-1203548561/|access-date=2020-09-21|website=WWD|language=en}}</ref> They also signed an agreement in July 2020 with a high-end Italian jewelry group to develop the [[Damiani (jewelry company)|Damiani]] and Salvini brands in China.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Zhang|first1=Tianwei|date=2020-07-10|title=Fosun's Jewelry Unit Yuyuan Scores Damiani Group China License|url=https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/fosun-jewelry-unit-yuyuan-scores-damiani-group-china-license-1203672198/|access-date=2020-09-21|website=WWD|language=en}}</ref> In August 2020, the company bought a 30% stake in Jinhui Liquor for $262 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chinese conglomerate Fosun's Yuyuan to buy 30% stake in Jinhui Liquor for $262m|url=https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/fosun-yuyuan-jinhui-liquor-196315/|access-date=2020-09-21|website=DealStreetAsia|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022, after has been severely hit by the effects of the [[COVID-19 lockdown in China|COVID-19 pandemic and China's extreme lockdown policies]], the Shanghai-based conglomerate divested many of its key assets to avoid defaulting on its short-term debts. By October 2022, Fosun announced that it would sell as much as $11 billion of assets within the next 12 months, amid efforts to bolster both its balance sheet and investor confidence.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-10-25 |title=China's Fosun Aims to Sell $11 Billion of Assets in Next Year |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-10-25/china-s-fosun-aims-to-sell-11-billion-of-assets-in-next-year |access-date=2023-02-24}}</ref>

== Response to COVID-19 pandemic ==
During the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic of 2020]], Fosun Pharmaceuticals partnered with German biotech firm Biopharmaceutical New Technologies ([[BioNTech]]) to produce and distribute the [[COVID-19]] [[mRNA vaccine]] [[BNT162b2]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fosun and BioNTech launch $135m vaccine hunt for coronavirus |url=https://www.ft.com/content/271ee270-6796-11ea-800d-da70cff6e4d3 |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Exclusive: Fosun and Germany's BioNTech to Make Vaccine in China - Caixin Global |url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2020-12-30/exclusive-fosun-will-partner-with-germanys-biontech-to-make-covid-vaccine-in-china-101645084.html |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=www.caixinglobal.com |language=en}}</ref> The company also donated medical supplies to several countries during the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flannery |first=Russell |title=Act Globally: China's Fosun International Guo Guangchang On Lessons From COVID-19 Pandemic |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/russellflannery/2020/04/15/act-globally-chinas-fosun-international-guo-guangchang-on-lessons-from-covid-19-pandemic/ |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=From China to the World, Fosun's Fight against COVID-19 Continues |url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/from-china-to-the-world-fosun-s-fight-against-covid-19-continues-1029072113 |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=markets.businessinsider.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Shareholders==
The major shareholder of Fosun International was a Hong Kong incorporated company Fosun Holdings,<ref name=FosunIntl2015AR/> which was a wholly owned subsidiary of [[British Virgin Islands]] incorporated company Fosun International Holdings. Three founders of Fosun International, [[Guo Guangchang]], [[Liang Xinjun]] and [[Wang Qunbin]], owned 64.45%, 24.44% and 11.11% respectively in Fosun International Holdings.<ref name=FosunIntl2015AR/> [[Fan Wei (entrepreneur)|Fan Wei]], another founder, withdrew his stake in Fosun International Holdings in September 2015.<ref name=FosunIntl2015AR/>

extract: Fosun International Limited is a Chinese multinational conglomerate holding company. Founded in 1992 by Guo Guangchang and four others, the company is headquartered in Shanghai and was incorporated in Hong Kong in 2004. Its Co-CEOs are Chen Qiyu and Xu Xiaoliang. Wang Qunbin joined Guo Guangchang as co-chairman in early 2020. The company is located in over 35 countries and is one of the largest privately owned conglomerates in China. It was ranked 371st on the Forbes Global 2000 ranking in 2020.
